cases.description: When a non‑null ExecutionContext is provided and the validator’s keyword is non‑null, the method should delegate to collectAnnotations(ExecutionContext, String) and return the boolean result of that call (expected true for the happy‑path mock).
If the supplied ExecutionContext is null the method should guard against NPE and return false without delegating.
Validator returns a non‑null keyword (e.g., "type"). The overload should treat it as a normal keyword and return true.
Validator’s getKeyword() returns null. The method should detect the missing keyword and return false.
When the ExecutionContext signals that annotation collection is disabled, the method must short‑circuit and return false regardless of the keyword.

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext that throws RuntimeException when getAnnotations() is called

cases.description: If the underlying collectAnnotations(ExecutionContext, String) throws an exception, the wrapper method should propagate it (no swallow).

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext with collectAnnotationsEnabled = true and getKeyword() = "type"; collectAnnotations(ExecutionContext, "type") stubbed to return false

cases.description: When the ExecutionContext is valid and the validator provides a non‑null keyword, the wrapper should delegate to the overloaded collectAnnotations method and propagate its boolean result. The stubbed overload returns false, so the wrapper must also return false.
If the validator’s getKeyword() returns an empty string (""), the wrapper should treat it as a missing keyword and return false without delegating to the overload.

group: collectAnnotations - executionContext with immutable annotations map

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext with collectAnnotationsEnabled = true; its annotations map is immutable (Collections.emptyMap())

cases.description: Even though annotation collection is enabled, the underlying collectAnnotations(ExecutionContext, String) cannot add a new annotation because the map is immutable. The overload therefore returns false, and the wrapper must return false.

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext where isCollectAnnotationsEnabled() throws IllegalStateException

cases.description: If the ExecutionContext throws a checked (runtime) exception while the wrapper checks the collection flag, the exception should propagate unchanged; the method must not swallow it.
A subclass of BaseJsonValidator overrides getKeyword() to throw a RuntimeException. The wrapper should not catch it and must let the exception propagate.

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext where isCollectAnnotationsEnabled() throws NullPointerException

cases.description: When the ExecutionContext throws a NullPointerException while the wrapper checks the collection flag, the exception must propagate unchanged.

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext where isCollectAnnotationsEnabled() throws IllegalArgumentException

cases.description: If isCollectAnnotationsEnabled() throws an IllegalArgumentException, the wrapper should not swallow it and should propagate the same exception.

input.value: mocked ExecutionContext with collectAnnotationsEnabled = true; overload collectAnnotations(ExecutionContext, String) throws AssertionError

cases.description: The overloaded collectAnnotations method throws an AssertionError (a subclass of java.lang.Error). The wrapper must let the Error propagate without conversion.
